_meta.purpose: Ground truth for the Python sink-detector bench. Keyed <file>::<function>, valued with the sink-family code the function should produce, or "clean".
_meta.scope: Sink family ONLY: E0711 path, E0713 SQLi, E0714 command, E0718 open redirect, E0719 SSTI, E0720 deserialization, E0723 hardcoded credential, E0727 XXE. Capability findings (E0701) are NOT ground truth here - on Python the module policy is empty by construction, so every I/O call produces one; they are an inventory, not a verdict.
_meta.out_of_scope: The effect-string family (E0710/E0721/E0722 SSRF, cleartext) reads a DECLARED net.fetch annotation Python does not have, and the marker family (E0712/E0715/E0716/E0717/E0724) needs marker types Python has no annotation-free equivalent for. The requests/capitalone/pyjwt repros are therefore labelled clean for the sink family - that is correct, not a miss, and the report says so.
_meta.method: Hand-labeled by reading each function against its own header comment, which states the CWE and names the documented fix. The bench/realworld_* repros were written before this bench existed, for the Aether ports, so their labels were not chosen to flatter the frontend.
_meta.independence_caveat: Author-established ground truth (the repo's author wrote both the repros and the detectors). Same caveat as tools/py_corpus2/LABELS.json.
